title: API key is hard-coded in a script the browser downloads
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain <script src>. Lines 6 and 11 send the key as a Bearer token from the browser. Anyone who opens the page source or DevTools Network tab reads it. The value is a stripe-key placeholder, so a real key would sit in the same place. Traced.
failing_case: Open the deployed page, view source of api.js: the key is in plain text. With it the reader can call POST /refunds for any order ids without using the UI.
remediation: Move the key to a server-side proxy that adds the Authorization header and enforces who may refund. Rotate any key that was ever shipped in this file.

title: refund() never waits for the request and always reports success
evidence: Line 11 calls fetch without await and without a catch. Line 12 returns { ok: true } at once, whatever the network or server does. app.js:51 trusts r.ok and shows the success toast. Traced.
failing_case: Go offline, or make the server answer 403 or 500, select an order and click 'Refund selected'. The toast reads 'Refunded 1 orders!' and no refund happened. The rejected fetch is also an unhandled promise rejection.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return the parsed result or throw. In app.js catch the error and show the cause and a retry step; show success only after the server confirms.

title: Customer name is written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: Line 32 builds the row as an HTML string and assigns it with innerHTML +=. o.customer.name comes from the API (customer-supplied data). o.id is also placed inside an attribute unquoted-safe only by luck: data-id="${o.id}". Traced; no sanitiser anywhere in the payload.
failing_case: A customer registers with the name . When any user loads the dashboard, the script runs in the admin's session, with access to the page and the refund call.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent (or escape at this one sink), and set data-id through dataset. Do the same in the stats template.

title: Selection only ever grows: unchecking does not deselect, so unchecked orders get refunded
evidence: The handler pushes on check and does nothing on uncheck. selected is module-global, never cleared on page change, search, or after refund. renderTable rebuilds rows (checkboxes come back unchecked) while selected keeps the ids. Duplicates are possible. refund(selected) at line 50 sends the whole array. Traced.
failing_case: Tick order 12, untick it, tick order 15, click Refund: the request body is {"ids":["12","15"]}, so order 12 is refunded though the user cleared it. Also: tick an order, click Next, click Refund: the order on the earlier page is refunded though nothing is visibly selected.
remediation: Keep selected as a Set, add on check and delete on uncheck, restore checked state when rendering, clear it after a confirmed refund, and show the count next to the button.

quote: **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README claims WCAG 2.1 AA and 44 px targets; the page fails both, and 2.5.5 is not an AA criterion
evidence: Failures found in this review: span-as-button (index.html:19), outline removed (styles.css:19), contrast under 4.5:1 (styles.css:9), no labels, colour-only status, fixed-width table. 2.5.5 Target Size is Level AAA in WCAG 2.1, so it is not part of AA; the actual buttons are about 20 px tall (styles.css:18).
failing_case: A procurement or legal reader relies on the 'fully accessible' claim for a public-sector deployment and the page fails an audit.
remediation: Remove the claim until an audit passes, then state the conformance level and date; cite 2.5.5 as AAA or switch to 2.5.8 (WCAG 2.2 AA, 24 px).

quote: **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the key never leaves the server; the key is in the client bundle
evidence: api.js:3 defines API_KEY and api.js:6 and api.js:11 send it from the browser. Traced.
failing_case: A reader or security reviewer trusts the README, skips a key audit, and ships the page with the key exposed.
remediation: Fix the code (proxy the call), then keep the claim; or delete the claim until it is true.

quote: 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong, and the pricing has nothing to do with this app
evidence: $15 x 12 seats = $180 a month; x 12 months = $2,160 a year; less 20% = $1,728. $1,440 matches no reading: it is a 33% discount on $2,160, or $15 x 12 seats x 8 months. If $15 is per seat per year, the total is $180 or $144 after the discount. The line is also out of scope for an order dashboard README.
failing_case: A buyer quotes $1,440 from the README and is invoiced $1,728, or a seller under-quotes by $288 a year.
remediation: State the unit (per seat per month or year), recompute ($1,728 under the per-month reading), and move pricing out of the README into a source that owns it.

quote: - Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.
title: README says refunds are confirmed first; there is no confirmation step
evidence: app.js:49-51: the click handler calls refund(selected) immediately; no confirm(), dialog or second step exists in index.html or app.js. Traced.
failing_case: An operator relies on the confirmation to catch a mis-click, clicks the Refund control once, and a money-moving request is sent at once.
remediation: Add the confirmation (count and total, Cancel and Refund buttons), or remove the claim.

title: Pagination skips the first ten orders and is off by one
evidence: page starts at 1 (line 3) but start = page * PAGE_SIZE, so the first view shows orders 10-19. Orders 0-9 are only reachable by pressing Prev to page 0. The label on line 34 uses Math.floor(length / 10), which gives 'Page 1 of 2' for 25 orders that need 3 pages, and 'Page 1 of 0' for under 10 orders. Traced.
failing_case: With 25 orders: first load shows orders 10-19 labelled 'Page 1 of 2'. Orders 0-9 and the last partial page are never labelled as pages. With 5 orders the table is empty and the label says 'Page 1 of 0'.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE and Math.ceil(length / PAGE_SIZE) with a minimum of 1.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot
evidence: The Status cell holds an empty span coloured green, red or yellow (styles.css:17) with no text, title or aria-label. Red/green is the classic colour-blind pair. WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color (A) and 1.1.1. Traced.
failing_case: A red-green colour-blind user cannot tell paid from refunded; a screen-reader user hears an empty cell. This is the column that decides which order to refund.
remediation: Print the status word next to the dot (and give the dot aria-hidden), keeping the colour as a secondary cue.

title: Responses are applied in arrival order, one request per keystroke, with no error handling
evidence: app.js:45 binds load to every input event. app.js:41 assigns whichever response lands last and never checks that it still matches the current input. api.js:7 calls res.json() with no res.ok check, and load() has no try/catch.
failing_case: Type 'ab': the 'a' response arrives after the 'ab' response and the table shows results for 'a' under a box that says 'ab'. A 500 or an HTML error page makes res.json() throw an unhandled rejection: the table and stats stay stale and no message appears.
remediation: Debounce the input and use an AbortController or request counter so only the latest response applies. Check res.ok and show an error with a retry.

title: Search box, status filter and row checkboxes have no accessible name
evidence: No <label>, aria-label or aria-labelledby on #q (line 17) or #status (line 18). The row checkboxes at app.js:32 have no name, and the first <th> (index.html:21) is empty. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2 and 4.1.2. Placeholder disappears on typing and is not a reliable name. Traced.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'combo box' with no purpose, and 'checkbox' for every row with no hint of which customer it refunds.
remediation: Add <label for="q">Search customers</label> (or aria-label), label the select 'Status', and give each checkbox aria-label="Select order {id} for {name}" (set via setAttribute, not string concatenation).

title: Muted text fails contrast: card labels, buttons and the eyebrow
evidence: Computed: #aaa on white 2.32:1 (.lbl, styles.css:9), #aaa on #F4F1EA 2.06:1 (pager buttons, styles.css:18), #c7c2f0 on #6366f1 2.64:1 (.eyebrow, styles.css:4). Text is 11-12 px. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) needs 4.5:1. Refund button white on #8b5cf6 is 4.23:1, also under 4.5.
failing_case: A user with low vision cannot read REVENUE, ORDERS, AVG ORDER labels or the Prev and Next buttons.
remediation: Use #595959 or darker for muted text, 14 px or larger, and a darker purple (such as #6d3fd6) behind white text.

title: Table has a fixed 1000 px width and the three stat cards never stack
evidence: At 390 px the table is 1000 px wide inside a main with 24 px padding, so the page scrolls sideways. No media queries exist in styles.css. .cards is repeat(3, 1fr) at every width (line 6), so each card is about 100 px wide with 32 px numbers. At 200% zoom (about 640 CSS px) the same overflow occurs. WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA). Traced; not rendered.
failing_case: Open the page on a 390 px phone: the user must scroll horizontally to see the Status column and the refund checkboxes; the stat numbers wrap or clip.
remediation: Use width: 100% with an overflow-x: auto wrapper for the table, and @media (max-width: 600px) { .cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }.

title: Focus outline removed from every interactive control with no replacement
evidence: The rule removes the default ring on buttons, inputs and selects. No :focus-visible style exists anywhere in styles.css. WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA). Traced.
failing_case: Tab to Prev, Next, the search box or the status select: nothing on screen shows where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid <colour with 3:1 contrast>; outline-offset: 2px; }.

title: getOrders never checks the HTTP status
evidence: No res.ok check before res.json(). A 401, 429 or 500 error body is returned as if it were the order list. app.js:41 assigns it to orders, then renderStats calls `for (const o of orders)`, which throws on a non-iterable object. There is no try/catch in load(). Traced.
failing_case: The server answers 401 with {"error":"unauthorized"}. orders becomes that object; renderStats throws 'orders is not iterable'; the table and cards keep the previous data and the user sees no message.
remediation: Throw on !res.ok, and in load() catch and render an error state that names the failure and offers Retry. Validate that the body is an array.

title: Load failures are unhandled, and an empty result renders NaN
evidence: There is no try/catch around the await, so a network error or an error JSON body leaves the old table in place (or throws inside renderStats if the body is not an array). On an empty result, avg = revenue / orders.length (app.js:18) is 0/0, so the card reads '$NaN'. There is no empty state; the table is blank and the pager reads 'Page 1 of 0'.
failing_case: Search 'zzz' with no matches: AVG ORDER shows $NaN and the user sees an empty grid. With the API down, the user sees stale data and no message.
remediation: Wrap load in try/catch with a visible error and retry; guard the divide; render 'No orders match' with a hint to clear the filter.

title: Refund fires immediately with no confirmation, though the README says refunds are confirmed
evidence: app.js:49-52 is the handler; no confirm dialog or second step exists in index.html or app.js. README.md:9 claims confirmation. Refunds move money and cannot be undone from the UI.
failing_case: A misclick on 'Refund selected' sends the refunds for the whole selection at once. With nothing selected it still posts { ids: [] } and shows 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
remediation: Disable the control when nothing is selected. Ask for confirmation naming the count and total. Disable it while the request is in flight, and send an idempotency key.

title: Refund has no confirmation, no empty guard, no double-click guard, and the toast never clears
evidence: The click handler (line 49) calls refund immediately, though README.md:9 says refunds are confirmed first. Nothing disables the control while the request is pending; selected is not cleared, so a second click sends the same ids again. With nothing selected the handler still reports 'Refunded 0 orders!'. The toast has no timeout. Traced.
failing_case: Select one order, click Refund twice quickly: two POST /refunds with the same ids go out, and the toast says 'Refunded 1 orders!'. Click with no selection: 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
remediation: Show a confirm step naming the count and total, disable the control while pending, send an idempotency key, refuse an empty selection, clear selected on success, and hide the toast after a few seconds.

title: The Refund control is a span: no keyboard access, no role, no name for assistive tech
evidence: A span is not focusable and has no role=button. app.js:49 attaches only onclick. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A). Traced.
failing_case: Tab through the page with the keyboard: focus skips the Refund control and Enter/Space never reach it. A keyboard or screen-reader user cannot perform the main task of the page.
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn">Refund selected</button> and restyle the .refund class on it.

quote: // compute revenue: paid minus refunds, with 8.25% tax and the loyalty discount for gold customers
title: Tax rate, loyalty discount and revenue rule live inside a render function, in floating point
evidence: Lines 11-17 apply a 10% gold discount (0.9), an 8.25% tax (1.0825) and sign by status inside renderStats. Money is a JS float, rounded only at display. The table (line 32) shows raw o.total with no tax or discount, so the revenue card does not reconcile to the rows. The rule exists nowhere else and has no test. Tax is added on top of o.total, which is probably already a total. Traced.
failing_case: One gold customer, one paid order of 100: the row shows $100, the REVENUE card shows $97.43 (100*0.9*1.0825). Finance reads two different numbers for the same order.
remediation: Move the rule to one pure function (e.g. orderRevenue(order)) with unit tests, compute in integer cents or take the amount from the server, and let the view only format the result. State whether total already includes tax and discount.

title: An empty result shows $NaN and no empty state
evidence: app.js:18 divides by orders.length; 0/0 is NaN and app.js:22 renders avg.toFixed(2) as '$NaN'. No empty message exists for the table.
failing_case: Type a search that matches nothing: the AVG ORDER card reads $NaN and the table body is blank with no explanation.
remediation: Guard the empty case, show '$0.00' or a dash, and render a 'No orders match' row with a hint to clear the filters.

title: Prev and Next are unbounded and the page is not reset on a new search
evidence: No lower or upper clamp on page, and the buttons are never disabled. load() (line 38) does not reset page. A negative page gives a negative slice start, which slices from the end of the array. Traced.
failing_case: Click Prev twice: page is -1 and slice(-10, 0) is empty; label reads 'Page -1'. Go to a later page, then type a search that returns 8 results: the table is empty because page is still past the end.
remediation: Clamp page to [1, lastPage], disable Prev/Next at the ends, and set page = 1 in load().

title: Refund can be submitted repeatedly, empty, with no in-flight state or idempotency key
evidence: The handler is not disabled during the call and sends whatever selected holds, even []. The selected list is not cleared (app.js:50-51). The request carries no idempotency key (api.js:11). The toast is never hidden (app.js:51). Traced.
failing_case: Double-click Refund selected with 2 orders ticked: two POSTs are sent with the same ids, and the second toast overwrites the first.
remediation: Disable the button while pending, ignore empty selections, send an idempotency key, clear the selection, and hide the toast after a few seconds.

title: Toast has no live region and is never dismissed
evidence: index.html:23 has no role="status" or aria-live. app.js:51 sets display:block and nothing ever hides it again or clears it. The refund error path writes nothing at all. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA).
failing_case: A screen-reader user hears nothing after pressing Refund. A sighted user sees 'Refunded 2 orders!' stay forever, even after a later refund fails.
remediation: Add role="status" (or role="alert" for failures), update text for both outcomes, and hide it after a timeout or on a close button.

quote: button { border: 0; background: none; color: #aaa; padding: 2px 4px; font-size: 12px; }
title: Prev and Next are tiny text-only buttons that do not look like buttons
evidence: 12 px text with 2 px/4 px padding gives targets about 20 px tall. No border, no background, no hover or active style, and the text is low contrast. Row checkboxes are default size. This is unrelated to the pass/fail of 2.5.5 (AAA) but breaks the README's own 44 px claim and is under 24 px (2.5.8 in WCAG 2.2). Traced.
failing_case: On a phone, a user taps Next and hits the wrong row or nothing; the button gives no visible pressed state.
remediation: Give the buttons a visible border or fill, at least 44 px height on touch, 14 px or larger text, and hover, active and disabled styles.

title: Toast pulses forever and ignores reduced-motion
evidence: The animation runs infinitely while the toast is visible and the toast is never hidden (app.js:51). No prefers-reduced-motion media query in the file. WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) for motion over 5 s, and 2.3.3 guidance. Traced.
failing_case: After one refund, the toast keeps pulsing until the page is reloaded, including for users who set 'reduce motion'.
remediation: Remove the infinite pulse (or run it once), and wrap any motion in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

title: Search text is put into the URL without encoding
evidence: query comes straight from the #q input (app.js:39) and is concatenated into the query string. No encodeURIComponent. Traced.
failing_case: Type `smith&status=refunded#` in the search box: the request becomes /orders?q=smith&status=refunded#&status=... The fragment drops the real status filter and the user's text changes other parameters. A search for `a&b` or `50%` returns the wrong results.
remediation: Use new URL() with searchParams.set('q', query) and searchParams.set('status', status), or wrap each value in encodeURIComponent.

title: Performance claim has no measurement and the code does not support it
evidence: load() downloads every order on every keystroke (app.js:45) with no debounce; renderStats walks all orders (app.js:11); the table renders only a page of 10, but rows are built with innerHTML += (app.js:32). No benchmark or test in the payload. 'Instantly' is not a figure.
failing_case: With 10,000 orders each keystroke fetches and parses the full list and recomputes stats; on a slow link the box lags and responses interleave.
remediation: Page and filter on the server, debounce, and either measure and state the number (ms at N orders, device) or remove the claim.
